daily.title: Delhi HC: Nil Certificate for India-US DTAA Matching Solutions
daily.summary: Delhi High Court directs NIL TDS certificate for Matching Solutions under India-US DTAA, setting aside 15% rate. Learn more. Brief : A US company supplying foreign exchange matching solutions and support services to its Indian group entity applied for a Nil certificate under Section 197. The Competent Authority issued a certificate at 15%, treating the receipts as fees for included services under Article 12(4) of the India-US DTAA. daily.title: Outstanding Sundry Creditors Cannot Be Treated as Cessation of Liability Without Evidence, Holds ITAT
daily.summary: The ITAT has held that Ad Hoc addition under Section 41(1) was prejudicial to the assessee and not Revenue. Aggrieved by the revisionary order, the assessee approached the Tribunal, contending that the PCIT had wrongly assumed jurisdiction under Section 263. The Tribunal observed that the PCIT had correctly recognised that the Income Tax Act does not permit an ad hoc disallowance of a fixed percentage of total sundry creditors. The Tribunal explained that sundry creditors represent liabilities appearing in the balance sheet and not current-year income or expenditure.
